title: DoorLens
oneLiner: A local tool that classifies recorded train-door movements and tests whether a result holds up.
shortSummary: Nebula X 2026 hackathon submission (PS3). Classifies recorded door movements with a frozen model, re-runs a cycle under explicit synthetic recording changes, and ranks a train’s air-conditioning units by refrigerant-leak likelihood.
responsibilities: Built the FastAPI backend that validates uploads, segments cycles and runs frozen-model inference
Built the Next.js and Plotly front end, served as a static export by the same API
Added “challenge this result” probes that copy and rescale a cycle and re-run the same model
Wrote model-parity, API and browser verification scripts
constraints: The test data had no ground truth, so it was used only for format checks and inference, never for fitting
Runs entirely locally: no database, cloud service, authentication or external AI API
outcomes: 32 Python tests passed and frozen-model parity reproduced across 2,091 comparisons
Sensitivity probes never alter the original prediction exports
